transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Broadband faults desk, my name is Keith.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Keith, my name is Rory McAllister. Whenever anyone in our household turns on the kitchen microwave oven to heat up food or boil a cup of soup, our Wi-Fi broadband connection drops dead instantly across every phone and television in the house, and only reconnects three minutes after the microwave stops!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon Rory. If I understand correctly, your Wi-Fi broadband connection drops completely every time your kitchen microwave oven is turned on and takes several minutes to recover. Before we test your connection, could you confirm your full postal address and your account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 45 Braemar Terrace, Aberdeen, AB10 7EJ, security PIN 6620, router model S-Net Hub 4.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Rory, that confirms your account details. Where is your broadband router physically located in relation to the kitchen microwave?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The router sits on a bookshelf in our open-plan living room, about four meters away from the microwave with only a plasterboard partition wall in between.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could I place you on hold for two minutes while I query your router's wireless spectrum interference and signal-to-noise ratio logs?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Rory. The wireless radio telemetry confirms acute microwave radio frequency radiation leakage centered on 2450 megahertz.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why does microwave cooking radiation knock out our internet?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Domestic microwave magnetrons emit high-powered radio waves at 2450 MHz, which precisely overlaps Wi-Fi channels 8, 9, and 10 on the 2.4 GHz spectrum.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you configure the router so it is completely immune to kitchen appliances?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you operate a faulty, unshielded microwave oven with deteriorated door seals that leaks radiation into living areas, that is a domestic appliance hazard, not an S-Net telecommunications fault.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our microwave is a certified Panasonic oven bought brand new last year! Don't tell me my kitchen is hazardous when your router can't handle a microwave!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am explaining how electromagnetic radiation from aging magnetrons overwhelms 2.4 GHz receiver antennas.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What can we adjust on the router to prevent these drops?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The router operating frequency can be reconfigured across our remote network management portal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Keith? Hello? The line went completely dead for over thirty seconds! Did we get disconnected?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I was querying the 5 GHz radio availability on your S-Net Hub 4.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please separate the 5 GHz network from the 2.4 GHz network so our devices avoid the microwave.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously 5 GHz wireless spectrum operates between 5180 MHz and 5825 MHz, completely immune to microwave oven magnetron emissions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly! So please separate the 5 GHz network right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Rory speaking, my teenage daughter is studying for her Scottish Advanced Higher examinations, and her timed online mock exam was abruptly terminated and scored as zero yesterday because my wife turned on the microwave to warm soup! My daughter was in floods of tears, terrified she will fail her university entrance requirements! Having your family's future jeopardized because heating soup cuts the Wi-Fi is unacceptable! We need this solved!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how devastating and stressful that was for your daughter and your entire family, Rory, especially with university entrance examinations and mock exams at stake. Having timed exam sessions terminated over cooking appliances is deeply upsetting, and I will reconfigure your router onto clean 5 GHz frequencies right now to protect her exams.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Keith. What steps are required?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am splitting your S-Net Hub 4 Wi-Fi broadcast into separate SSIDs: 'S-Net-McAllister-2.4' and 'S-Net-McAllister-5G'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The router light blinked orange and is now steady green.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your daughter's laptop and household smartphones must be connected exclusively to 'S-Net-McAllister-5G'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am connecting her laptop to 'S-Net-McAllister-5G' right now... Connected with full signal bars!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because 5 GHz operates gigahertz away from magnetron frequencies, microwave emissions cannot induce packet loss on that SSID.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can we test turning on the microwave right now while she is on 5 GHz to prove it doesn't disconnect?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because running an empty microwave oven causes magnetron arcing damage, testing requires heating a bowl of water or food during active cooking cycles.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My wife and daughter are out at the library until six o'clock this evening, and I don't want to run the oven until dinner time.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You will need to verify the connection when you use the microwave during dinner preparation tonight.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So we cannot confirm right now while we are on this call that the drops have completely stopped?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Keith? Hello? Why does your telephone line keep dropping into total silence for thirty or forty seconds?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I was documenting your wireless channel separation under case reference RF-MICROWAVE-88192-A.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: RF-MICROWAVE-88192-A, noted down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Keep all examination laptops and streaming devices locked to the 5 GHz network to prevent future interference.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will ensure her laptop forgets the 2.4 GHz network so it never roams back.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also adjusted the 2.4 GHz channel to channel 1, which sits furthest away from the 2450 MHz magnetron peak.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That provides extra buffer for legacy 2.4 GHz smart plugs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just making sure our premises records match perfectly: that was 44 Lenton Boulevard, Nottingham, wasn't it?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 44 Lenton Boulevard, Nottingham.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Rory, that confirms the premises record on the diagnostic profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will test the microwave at six o'clock tonight when heating dinner.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have documented your account notes with a follow-up advisory.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Keith for splitting those networks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also waived this month's router rental fee as a courtesy for your daughter's exam disruption.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is appreciated. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there any other broadband issue I can assist with today, Rory?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No Keith, that covers it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.text: Goodbye.
